# Abstract {.unnumbered .inn-next-page}

<!--
A PhD dissertation must have one summary in Norwegian and one in English, each
no longer than a page. The `.inn-next-page` class lets this one open on the
page after the Norwegian summary, whichever side that is, so that the two land
on pages i and ii as the university asks.
-->

**Background.** Regular physical activity is associated with a lower risk of
cardiometabolic disease, but the dose–response relationship in older adults is
not well characterised.

**Methods.** Sixty-two community-dwelling adults aged 65–79 years completed a
12-week supervised training intervention. The primary outcome was change in
peak oxygen uptake.

**Results.** Peak oxygen uptake increased by 2.4 mL·kg⁻¹·min⁻¹ (95% CI
1.6 to 3.2) in the intervention group relative to control.

**Conclusion.** A 12-week supervised programme produced clinically relevant
improvements in cardiorespiratory fitness.

*Keywords:* physical activity, ageing, cardiorespiratory fitness
